ai.name: DeepSeek
ai.hook: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash, matching near-frontier scores at 60% lower cost per task.
insights: **Terminal-Bench score of 82.7**, close to GPT-5.6 Luna's 51 while costing far less per task
**284B total / 13B active parameters**, 1M context length, open weights under **MIT license**
Supports **4-bit and 3-bit quantization** for local deployment, $0.14/M input and $0.27/M output pricing
ai.for_you: This is the kind of model to test as a cheap backend for your PT SMB agency's agentic workflows, MIT license means no legal friction reselling it inside client automations.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only real model release today, confirmed across three independent sources

ai.name: Model Context Protocol
ai.hook: MCP 2.0 drops statelessness, the biggest spec change since launch.
insights: Called **'Stateless MCP day'** by the community, the 2026-07-28 spec revision
Simon Willison built **mcp-explorer** and **datasette-mcp** immediately to test it
Removes the persistent-connection requirement that made MCP hard to deploy at enterprise scale
ai.for_you: If you're wiring client-facing agents for PT SMBs, stateless MCP means simpler serverless tool integrations, worth a quick spike before committing to a specific agent framework this quarter.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most substantive protocol-level change in Simon Willison's week, direct implication for agent tooling

ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: Codex unexpectedly took off among OpenAI's own non-developers, reshaping ChatGPT Work.
insights: Same **agent harness** now powers both Codex and ChatGPT Work internally
Employees describe using Codex as feeling like **'a new superpower'** even without coding background
OpenAI's bet: ideas and taste become the bottleneck once anyone can build, not code
ai.for_you: This validates your own positioning, you're not a developer but you're building real products, this is exactly the wedge OpenAI is designing ChatGPT Work around.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most detailed non-technical-founder AI story this week, directly mirrors Pedro's own profile

ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: GPT-5.6 Luna price cut 80%, agent workflow costs drop roughly 10x.
insights: **Sol Fast** tier offers 2.5x lower latency at double the price for latency-sensitive agents

ai.for_you: Agentic workflows for your agency clients just got structurally cheaper to run, worth re-pricing any GPT-5-based automation proposals you've quoted in the past month.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Direct cost impact on anything built on OpenAI's stack, confirmed across TLDR and AINews

ai.name: Interconnects (Nathan Lambert)
ai.hook: Open-weight models face a genuine '6 months to live' test against closed labs.
insights: Kimi K3's 2.8T params force a real reckoning on whether open-weight can sustain frontier pace

Zyphra, Cohere, and Poolside are diversifying the open ecosystem beyond the big labs
ai.for_you: No direct action here, but worth tracking since your agency's cost structure depends on which open models stay viable and cheap to self-host for PT clients wary of sending data to US clouds.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most sustained analytical thread this week across Interconnects' five posts

ai.name: MIT Technology Review
ai.hook: A fundamental flaw makes LLMs impossible to fully secure against hacks, researchers argue at ICML.
insights: Paper presented at a top AI conference claims the vulnerability is structural, not fixable with patches
Directly relevant given the same week's Anthropic and OpenAI agent-breach incidents
ai.for_you: If you're pitching agentic automation to PT SMBs, build in a 'no autonomous access to sensitive systems without human approval' clause now, this is becoming an unavoidable sales conversation.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only genuinely new security research finding today, not a repeat of the Anthropic/OpenAI incident stories

build_this.name: smevals
build_this.what_it_is: A small eval suite for testing models, prompts, and agent harnesses side by side.
build_this.why_try_it: Before you commit to DeepSeek-V4-Flash or any cheaper model for an agency client's workflow, run their actual prompts through this to verify quality doesn't drop, it's built exactly for this decision.

build_this.name: llm-mcp-client
build_this.what_it_is: A command-line client for talking to MCP servers using the new stateless 2026-07-28 spec.
build_this.why_try_it: Spin this up to see how a stateless MCP server would connect a client's existing tools (invoicing, CRM) to an agent, worth a one-afternoon prototype for your next SMB pitch deck.

build_this.name: qm (multiplayer agent harness)
build_this.what_it_is: An agent harness designed for multiple people to collaborate with an AI agent on shared work.
build_this.why_try_it: Your agency's core pitch to PT SMBs is often 'a team using AI together,' this repo is directly aimed at that exact multiplayer-agent use case, worth a read before your next client onboarding flow design.

podcasts.episode: OpenAI's Plan to Make ChatGPT the Everything App — Akshay Nathan, OpenAI
podcasts.takeaway: OpenAI is betting that ideas and taste, not coding skill, become the real bottleneck once agents can build anything.
key_points: Codex and ChatGPT Work share the same agent harness but aren't identical experiences by design
Agents now gather context across code, Slack, documents, and local files automatically
Teams are replacing decks and spreadsheets with interactive websites built by agents
podcasts.for_you: This is close to your own trajectory, non-developer building real products, worth watching in full for concrete examples of what 'generalist with a specialty' workflows look like in practice for your agency's own operations.

podcasts.episode: Can AI Startups Still Compete With the Labs?
